title: [P5 blocker] Make DirectTarget GitHub CLI compatible with native PR delivery
body:
## Outcome

Make the P5 DirectTarget image use a GitHub CLI version compatible with the pinned Zeroshot 10.3.0 native pull-request delivery path, and fail preflight before admission when that compatibility is absent.

This is required before freezing or dispatching another prospective P5 cohort. It does not reopen or replace the consumed v5 R01.

## Demonstrated problem

The retained [v5 R01 evidence](https://github.com/faviann/broodling/blob/445c6d773ab772cb00f98a274d4bb8fce3e21b84/evaluation/p5/runs/2026-09-19-v5-r01/README.md) classifies R01 as `IF`. Durable Zeroshot run `01a0b7e7-712e-7e42-9e6b-d0d0a2dec6ea` shows native delivery invoking:

```text
/usr/bin/gh api graphql --paginate --slurp ...
```

The selected DirectTarget image installs Debian's GitHub CLI 2.23.0, whose `gh api` has no `--slurp` flag. Delivery created and updated the authorized branch and [PR #2](https://github.com/faviann/broodling-p5-v3-20260917/pull/2), then its status query failed with `unknown flag: --slurp`; Zeroshot returned no successful receipt and Broodling recorded no disposition. A downloaded GitHub CLI 2.101.0 binary exposed the required flag, confirming the compatibility cause.

## Work

- Change the selected DirectTarget image definition to install and pin a GitHub CLI release that supports every CLI feature used by pinned Zeroshot 10.3.0 native PR delivery, including `gh api --slurp`.
- Add the smallest pre-admission compatibility check that records the installed `gh` version and refuses before a counted trial if `gh api --slurp` is unavailable.
- Validate the image and check without starting a provider task or using a frozen P5 slot.
- Preserve the v5 evidence, partial PR, quarantined Attempt and durable target state unchanged.

Keep this scoped to the DirectTarget GitHub CLI dependency and its preflight. Do not redesign delivery, change the provider/model/runtime, repair or merge the partial PR, or rerun R01.

## Completion

- The rebuilt target reports the pinned compatible `gh` version and `gh api --help` exposes `--slurp`.
- The preflight has a regression test or deterministic fixture proving an incompatible CLI is rejected before admission.
- Supported validation passes with no live provider inference.
- A later P5 run requires a separately reviewed prospective protocol/cohort and fresh authorization; this issue alone authorizes none.
